datasets.task_type: open-ended text generation for cultural awareness evaluation
datasets.annotation_method: Prompt templates designed by researchers and validated by 15 native speakers (at least one per language). Entity extraction from model outputs performed automatically by GPT-4o-mini. Entity linking to Wikidata is fully automatic. Manual evaluation of extraction quality conducted by native speakers on sampled data (50 sentences × 6 topics × 4 languages).

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: MaiNLP, Center for Information and Language Processing, LMU Munich; Munich Center for Machine Learning (MCML)
data_creator_info.evidence: 15 native speakers participated in prompt validation (at least one per language). Native speakers who validated prompts and annotated extraction quality include speakers of German, Spanish (Spain & Mexico), English (American & British), Turkish, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Thai, Chinese (Mainland), and Italian. All annotators were native speakers with graduate-level education background.

datasets.notes: MAKIEVAL is a framework rather than a static benchmark. It uses template-based prompts (Neutral, Explicit, Implicit) across 6 topics (food, beverages, clothing, books, music, transportation) and 19 countries/regions. Each prompt generates 500 responses per model. Total: 1,716 unique prompts, over 85.8 million generated texts across 7 evaluated models, 24,042 matched Wikidata cultural entities. Hausa and Yoruba were explored but excluded due to poor generation quality from open-source models.
